scenes.heading: Data, chance and logic problems
scenes.say: Graphs, Venn diagrams, dice and logic puzzles — these questions reward careful reading more than big calculations. Read, organise, then calculate.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Counting guests at a party who are on two different invite lists
scenes.science: In a Venn diagram, people in both groups go in the overlap — count them once
scenes.breaks: a party list has names to check; in a Venn question you only have the numbers.
scenes.say: Imagine counting party guests from two invite lists. Anyone on both lists must be counted only once. That's exactly what the overlap in a Venn diagram is for.

scenes.heading: Fill a Venn diagram from the middle
scenes.say: Forty people: twenty-two own a cat, fifteen a dog, six both. First the two circles, then six in the middle. Only cat is sixteen, only dog is nine. That's thirty-one with a pet, so nine own neither.
scenes.caption: 40 people: 22 own a cat, 15 a dog, 6 both. Six goes in the middle. Only cat is 16, only dog is 9. That's 31 with a pet, so 9 own neither.

scenes.heading: Read the graph, then calculate
scenes.say: Now a column graph of books read. Read each bar: six, four, nine and five. The total is twenty-four, so the mean is twenty-four divided by four, which is six. The range is nine minus four, which is five.

scenes.heading: Probability
scenes.say: Probability is the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of equally likely outcomes. Two dice give thirty-six outcomes. And if you don't replace the first pick, the bag shrinks.
scenes.caption: Probability = favourable outcomes ÷ total equally likely outcomes. Two dice give 36 outcomes. If you don't replace the first pick, the bag shrinks.

scenes.heading: A logic puzzle
scenes.question: Mo finished before Kai. Jo finished after Kai but before Lu. Who came last?
lines: Jo after Kai: Mo, Kai, Jo
Lu after Jo: Mo, Kai, Jo, Lu
scenes.say: For ordering puzzles, draw a line. Mo finished before Kai. Jo came after Kai but before Lu. Place them one clue at a time: Mo, Kai, Jo, Lu. So Lu came last.

points: Logic: draw a line or grid
scenes.say: Quick recap. Mean is total over count, and the median needs ordered data. Fill Venn diagrams from the middle, picture thirty-six outcomes for two dice, and draw your logic clues. Now try the practice questions!
